topic: Find further improvements to command surfacing after the planned phases 005 to 008: better UX for the person and the model (what the hook brief says, when a command is offered, asked or started, the install and setup path for an external repository), better performance (hook time, embedder cost, cold start, token cost of the brief) and above all usefulness across the six CLIs (claude, codex, opencode, pi, devin, dsh): whether a model on each runtime actually starts an offered command, and what stops it.

focus: The model-visible brief: measured payload, withheld document path, unobservable offer, and the argued-route scoring defect
Before-arm runtime behaviour: the policy split behind each start rate, the path-versus-outcome gap, and the policy that stops at the command
answeredQuestions: Which before-arm runtime behaviour explains the start rates (claude 3 of 12, codex 0 of 12, pi 0 of 12, devin 2 of 12 or 12, opencode 4 of 9, dsh 3 of 8), and what stops a model from starting an offered command?

focus: Per-runtime command discovery: the 12-command Claude loss, the three native spellings, and the missing visibility check
answeredQuestions: Which command-discovery surface defects (the g5 skill.md collision and its siblings) keep a command from being offered or found on each runtime, and what detects them before a user hits one?

focus: First run in an external repository: the skipped cold advisor, the first-start budget inversion, the shadowed hook config, and the spelling correction
answeredQuestions: What does a person installing Skilled into an external repository see on first run, and where does the setup path still fail silently after the embedder work phase 008 plans?

focus: The cost ledger: measured brief and hook cost, the invisible part, and the missing session total
answeredQuestions: What is the measured cost of the brief and of the hook (latency, tokens, cold start, embedder), and which part of that cost is invisible to the person paying it?
